Keep the camera nearly locked with only a tiny natural breathing drift; no forward rush, no vortex, no tunnel, no beam, no explosion, and no aggressive zoom. The people, lift, black railings, wall edges, and chamber texture gradually lose contrast, become weak silhouettes, then dissolve into the fog. Do not create any new UI, text, symbols, graphics, logos, or subtitles. Preserve the 35mm film look, low contrast, blue grey and cold white fog palette, soft halation, gentle film grain, and restrained cinematic haze. The last second should be a quiet full-screen cold white fog field with only very faint residual texture and no readable subjects. Audio is a deep low-frequency interior pressure tone, soft fog hiss, and very low room tone only. No music, no dialogue, no voice, no pops, no clicks, no impacts, and no sharp transient sounds.
